sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the style helpers and the input, textarea, and button parts. Nothing is shown on screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up the parts the group combines.

sections.name: InputGroup
sections.title: Outer box and attachment placement rules
sections.what: Builds the shared bordered box. Its rules change its height and layout when attachments sit at the top or bottom, and show focus and error rings around the whole group.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the whole group look like one field with a single focus and error state.
sections.watch_out: The focus and error rules rely on specific attribute names on the inner input, so renaming them breaks the highlight.

sections.name: InputGroupAddon
sections.title: Attachment area and click to focus
sections.what: Builds the attachment area for each side. Clicking the area, but not a button, moves keyboard focus to the first plain input in the group.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users click the attachment, such as an icon, to start typing.
sections.watch_out: Only a plain input receives this focus, so a group with a textarea will not respond to clicks.

sections.name: InputGroupButton
sections.title: Small buttons inside the group
sections.what: Builds compact buttons for use in attachments, with sizes from extra small to small and icon-only options. Buttons default to a type that does not submit forms.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps buttons small and prevents them from accidentally submitting a form.
sections.watch_out: Changing the default type to submit makes these buttons submit the form they sit inside.

sections.name: InputGroupText
sections.title: Plain text inside the group
sections.what: Builds a text label or icon holder for use inside an attachment, with muted color and small size.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows a unit or hint without making it look interactive.

sections.name: InputGroupInput
sections.title: Input inside the group
sections.what: Builds the input with no border or background so it blends into the outer box, and lets it grow to fill space.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the input seamless inside the shared box.

sections.name: InputGroupTextarea
sections.title: Textarea inside the group and exports
sections.what: Builds the multi-line text area with no border, a fixed look, and a vertical padding. The final list makes all parts available.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives longer text entries the same unified look.

summary: Builds a single bordered box that holds an input or textarea together with small attachments such as text, icons, or buttons on its sides.
purpose: Lets an input look like one unit with a unit or action attached to it, such as a currency sign or a search button.
why: Likely reason: attachments inside one shared border look cleaner than separate boxes. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the input, textarea, and button parts, and the style helpers. The outer box draws the shared border and ring. Its rules change based on where attachments sit. Attachments can go at the start, end, top, or bottom. Clicking an attachment moves focus to the input. Small buttons, text, the input, and the textarea each have their own part. Everything is exported.
inputs: Children such as an input, a textarea, text, icons, or buttons, plus an alignment setting for attachments and standard element settings.
outputs: A combined input box with attachments. Nothing is stored. Clicking the attachment area focuses the input.
risks: Clicking an attachment focuses the first plain input in the group only. A group with only a textarea will not receive that focus. Buttons default to a type that does not submit forms, so changing that can cause unexpected submissions.
debug: If the focus ring looks wrong, check the focus rules on the outer box. If a click on an attachment does nothing, check that the group contains a plain input. If a button submits a form unexpectedly, check its type setting.
